pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

examples.t: casa
examples.r: KAH-sah
examples.en: house

examples.t: mesa
examples.r: MEH-sah
examples.en: table

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.

examples.t: hola
examples.r: OH-lah
examples.en: hello

examples.t: jueves
examples.r: HWEH-vehs
examples.en: Thursday

rules.explain: Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.

examples.t: niño
examples.r: NEEN-yoh
examples.en: boy

examples.t: calle
examples.r: KAH-yeh
examples.en: street

rules.explain: Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).

examples.t: pero
examples.r: PEH-roh
examples.en: but

examples.t: perro
examples.r: PEH-rroh
examples.en: dog

rules.explain: Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

examples.t: gracias
examples.r: GRAH-syahs
examples.en: thanks

examples.t: café
examples.r: kah-FEH
examples.en: coffee

alphabet.title: The English alphabet: 26 letters
alphabet.explain: The alphabet you are reading now. Two notes for learners: the same letter can carry several sounds (the a in cake vs cat), and a few letters are silent in common words (the k in knife). You already know it — the rest of this course is about the sounds it makes.

letters.tip: k in cat, s in city
s in sun, sh in ship
t in time, ch in church

counting.title: Counting in English: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Learn 0-12 by heart — eleven, twelve and thirteen keep their old shapes; from fourteen the pattern ten + number holds.
rules: Stress falls on the first syllable of compound numbers: THIR-teen, not three-TEEN.
Th has two sounds: thin (sharp) vs this (soft).
R is optional in many accents — listen to British and American speakers and both are normal.
